title: Felix and the Letter
premise: In a colonial port city at the turn of the century, Oscar Sterling—daughter of a drowned pearl diver and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company—has survived by being unremarkable. When a census taker records her father's foreign birthright, she becomes evidence in a political purge, and the only person who can clear her name is Captain Elias Vane, her late father's sworn friend, now branded an enemy of the crown for refusing to surrender his fleet. Bound by a promise sealed in peacetime—a letter her father entrusted to Elias—Oscar must smuggle that letter through blockades, betrayals, and the company's own corruption to prove both their innocence. She succeeds at devastating cost: the letter exposes the governor's treason rather than her father's, toppling Meridian itself, and Oscar chooses found family over the restored name she never wanted.
about_author: Wren Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port-city shipping manifests and indenture ledgers before turning to fiction. They write about people history recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Opening on the pearl beds where her father drowned, then her gray routine as a tally clerk at Meridian Trading. Establishes her philosophy of invisibility: busy hands, lowered eyes. Emotional beat: grief worn down into habit.

chapters.title: Counted
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The census taker, Mr. Aldous Finch, arrives at the company dormitories and asks for parents' places of birth. Oscar lies; he writes something anyway. That night she finds her file pulled from the registry room. Beat: first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: What Papa Left
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Oscar's POV. Her father's last dive, his friendship with Captain Elias Vane of the coastal fleet, and the sealed letter he pressed into Elias's hands: 'If the company ever asks about my blood, give this to my girl.' Beat: love and foreboding.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She breaks into the registry after hours and discovers her entry flagged with a red thread—the mark used for enemy-blood investigations. A night watchman nearly catches her; she hides among cargo crates. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Captain Vane
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Introduced aboard the brig Fairwind, blockaded in harbor under new wartime edicts. He holds Oscar's letter still unopened, honoring a promise made over brandy years ago. His first mate urges him to burn it. Beat: loyalty tested by prudence.

chapters.title: Summons
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Company magistrate Hargrove summons her, questions her paternity with oily courtesy, and offers leniency if she denounces 'foreign sympathizers' among the dockworkers. She gives him nothing. Beat: the moment silence stops being safety.

chapters.title: Salt and Promises
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias learns from a bribed harbormaster that the girl Sterling is under investigation. He decides, against his crew's counsel, to get word to her. Beat: the promise becoming a debt he'll pay in full.

chapters.title: The Fishwife's Errand
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A message reaches her via Marta, a fishwife who knew her mother: meet a man at the salt sheds. Hope and terror war in her. She goes, watched by a company tail she doesn't spot. Beat: stepping off the safe path.

chapters.title: Two Strangers by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Oscar meets Silas, Elias's trusted deckhand, who tells her the captain holds her letter but cannot enter the city. She must bring proof of her identity to the blockade line—or trust a stranger with everything. Beat: faith as a gamble.

chapters.title: Hargrove's Web
chapters.summary: Hargrove's POV. Revealed: the purge isn't patriotic—it's cover for Hargrove and Governor Crane seizing independent fleets like the Fairwind. Oscar is bait to draw Elias ashore. Beat: villainy with a ledger-book face.

chapters.title: The Red Thread File
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She steals a copy of her own investigation file and learns her father was investigated once before—for witnessing a shipment Crane wanted buried. The letter may hold more than sentiment. Beat: personal stakes become dangerous knowledge.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas ferries Oscar out to the Fairwind past the blockade chain, a harrowing row through patrol boats. First sight of Elias in years. Beat: breathless hope.

chapters.title: The Unopened Letter
chapters.summary: Elias and Oscar's shared scene, Elias POV. Elias offers her the letter unopened—it was meant for her alone. She asks him to read it with her. Inside: not just words, but a bill of lading proving Crane smuggled arms under Meridian's flag. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Paper Proves
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They realize the letter can destroy Crane—but using it brands them traitors unless delivered to the right authority, and every official answerable to Crane. Beat: truth as a weapon that cuts its holder.

chapters.title: Return Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She slips back into the city before roll call, but Finch the census taker sees her return, wet-hemmed at dawn. He says nothing—yet. Beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: Finch's Question
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. The census taker, we learn, keeps his own private archive of irregularities—not from loyalty but obsession. He confronts Oscar gently: 'Who are you, really?' She lies badly. Beat: an unexpected mirror.

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Hargrove arrests Marta as a sympathizer to pressure Oscar. Guilt crushes her; the fishwife network goes silent. Beat: the cost of touching other lives.

chapters.title: The Crew Divided
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Aboard the Fairwind, half the crew wants to sell the letter back to Crane for pardons. Elias quashes a near-mutiny with quiet fury, losing his oldest friend, Boatswain Kerr, in the process. Beat: loyalty fracturing under fear.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Warehouse
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Desperate to free Marta, Oscar approaches Hargrove offering to deliver Elias's letter herself—as a trap. It's a bluff; she plans to hand him forged papers. Beat: the invisible girl learning to play visible games.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas, once a printer's apprentice, helps forge documents in the ship's hold. Intimate scenes of craft and fear; he and Oscar grow close. Beat: tenderness inside danger.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The warehouse exchange. Hargrove accepts the forgery, releases Marta—and then reveals he'd already verified the real letter's contents through a spy aboard the Fairwind. Oscar realizes the trap has inverted. Beat: triumph collapsing into horror.

chapters.title: Kerr's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Kerr's POV. The boatswain sold the letter's existence to save his own pension. Haunted, he watches soldiers board the Fairwind at dawn. Beat: cowardice examined without excuse.

chapters.title: Seized
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The Fairwind is impounded; Elias arrested for treason. He swallows the remaining copy of the bill of lading's location—his memory—rather than surrender it. Beat: stoic defiance.

chapters.title: Alone With It All
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Lowest point. Marta freed but broken, Elias in chains, Silas hunted, and Oscar blamed by the dockworkers for the raid. She considers fleeing on a northbound coaler. Beat: despair honestly rendered.

chapters.title: The Census Taker's Offer
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. Finch finds Oscar at the docks. He offers his private archive—years of Crane's irregularities—if she'll tell him the whole truth, on record. 'I count people,' he says. 'You're the first one who counted.' Beat: an unlikely alliance.

chapters.title: Reading the Archive
chapters.summary: Oscar and Finch's POV, alternating. In Finch's garret they reconstruct Crane's smuggling route from census anomalies, tax rolls, and missing ships. The pattern matches her father's final dive site. Beat: grief transformed into method.

chapters.title: Her Father's Last Dive
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar dives the wreck site herself, retrieving the physical manifest her father hid in the reef—the corroboration the letter needs. Nearly drowns; surfaces changed. Beat: reclaiming her inheritance from the sea.

chapters.title: Breaking Silas Out
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She and Finch spring Silas from the company lockup during a shift change, using forged transfer orders. Silas carries the recovered manifest toward sympathetic press in the capital. Beat: competence and camaraderie.

chapters.title: Hargrove Closes In
chapters.summary: Hargrove's POV. Hargrove traces the escape to Oscar and lays a public trap: Elias will be tried in the harbor square, and any sympathizer who speaks will hang beside him. Beat: the noose tightening visibly.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Quiet chapter. Oscar visits Marta, mends her father's diving knife, and writes her own letter—to whoever survives her. Silas returns early; they keep vigil together. Beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Trial in the Square
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Elias's trial becomes spectacle. Hargrove produces the forged papers as 'evidence,' confident. Elias refuses counsel and says only: 'Ask the girl what her father carried.' Beat: dignity as resistance.

chapters.title: Oscar Speaks
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Against every instinct, Oscar steps forward publicly—visible at last—and tells the story of the letter, the dive, the manifest. The crowd shifts; even Finch testifies with his archives. Beat: courage as choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: Crane's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Crane's POV (first appearance). The governor moves to dissolve the tribunal and declare martial law. For one black hour it seems force will simply erase the truth. Beat: power showing its naked face.

chapters.title: The Harbor Turns
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Dockworkers, fishwives, and loyal crew members blockade the tribunal with their bodies; Kerr, seeking redemption, produces his correspondence with Hargrove. The tide of witnesses becomes undeniable. Beat: ordinary people as the hinge of history.

chapters.title: Climax: The Manifest Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On the tribunal steps, Oscar reads her father's recovered manifest aloud—names, dates, Crane's signature. Soldiers waver; a junior officer arrests Hargrove when he orders fire on the crowd. Crane flees to his flagship. Beat: catharsis earned, not given.

chapters.title: What Power Does Afterward
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. Aftermath politics: Crane's patrons abandon him; he's quietly retired rather than hanged, which galls everyone. Oscar feels the hollowness of partial justice. Beat: disillusionment braided with relief.

chapters.title: Pardons and Conditions
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias is pardoned and offered a commission under the new administration—the same machinery, new paint. He declines and asks instead for the Fairwind and his crew's freedom. Beat: integrity intact.

chapters.title: The Letter, Finished
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar finally reads her father's letter's private pages—the words meant only for her, hidden beneath the evidence. Forgiveness, pride, permission to live loudly. She weeps for the first time since his death. Beat: grief finally allowed.

chapters.title: A Family Assembled
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The found family gathers: Elias as reluctant patriarch, Silas staying ashore, Marta reopening her stall, Finch invited to Sunday dinner despite his terrible manners. Oscar signs her own release from indenture. Beat: warmth after long cold.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. New Year's Eve on the harbor wall, fireworks over water where her father dove. Oscar, now a licensed salvager training other divers' children, keeps the letter framed above her desk. Final line: visibility, chosen, as freedom. Beat: resolution and open horizon.
